method.value: Fit 2D Gaussians to the 860 um continuum for nucleus and SF clump; integrate for flux; FWHM gives diameter

evidence.quote: We model the starburst nucleus as a Gaussian and define its diameter to be the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the resulting Gaussian fit
can be approximated to first order as spherical regions, to estimate their volume densities

validation.value: CO map fit gives sizes within 14% and 21%

evidence.quote: find an agreement with the $860\,\ensuremath{\mu}m$ continuum map for the sizes of the nucleus and the SF clump to within 14% and 21% respectively.

method.value: Sigma_SFR = SFRtot x (S860/S860tot)/A with SFRtot from SED fit

evidence.quote: $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SFR}}= \mathrm{SFR^{tot}} \times (S_{\,\nu,\,860\,\ensuremath{\mu}m}/S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\,\nu,\,860\,\ensuremath{\mu}m})/A$
We use a Monte Carlo analysis to estimate and propagate the uncertainties on all the parameters.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure turbulent velocity dispersion and Mach number

method.value: Fit and subtract local linear velocity gradient from CO(4-3) velocity map; Mach = sigma/cs

evidence.quote: Then, the turbulent Mach number is given by: $\mathcal{M}= \sigma_{v,\mathrm{turb}}/c_{\mathrm{s}}$.
Assuming the temperature of the molecular gas in the two regions to be between 10-100 K, we find the sound speed as $c_{\mathrm{s}} = 0.4\pm0.2\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$

validation.value: Independent 3DBarolo tilted-ring fit gives 13 and 23 km/s (18 after linear gradient in clump)

evidence.quote: The velocity dispersions we obtain for the nucleus and the SF clump are $13$ and $23\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ respectively.

findings_qualitative.value: The SF clump has intrinsic rotation distinct from galaxy-wide rotation.

evidence.quote: This implies that the SF clump has some intrinsic rotation of its own which is different than the systematic galaxy-wide rotation

claims.hypothesis: Does the KS relation reproduce measured Sigma_SFR in AzTEC-1?
claims.experiment: Predict Sigma_SFR from Sigma_gas via KS

evidence.quote: The relation underestimates the $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SFR}}$ in both regions by a factor 2-3.

claims.result: Underestimates by ~2 and 1.6 but within systematic uncertainties

evidence.quote: its predictions are consistent with the measured values when the systematic uncertainties are included

claims.hypothesis: Does turbulence-regulated SFK best predict SFR?
claims.experiment: Predict with SFK and compare across low- and high-z samples
claims.result: Agrees within uncertainties; overpredicts clump by 60%
claims.finding: SFK gives the best predictions; turbulence and gravity sustain high SFRs

evidence.quote: we conclude that the relation provides the best prediction for the SFR in low- and high-redshift star-forming regions.

why_this_data.value: Sub-kpc resolution of an unlensed starburst enables kinematic analysis of distinct regions

evidence.quote: In particular, we study the galaxy nucleus and an off-center star-forming (SF) clump in this galaxy because they have sufficient resolution to apply the kinematic analysis.

limitations_admitted.value: Large systematic uncertainties; magnetic field strength unknown; need larger sample
